title: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)

sections.label: Budget reduction motion
sections.summary: The Chairman is asked to move that the total sum allocated for Head I of the Estimates be reduced by $100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head I of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

sections.label: Social spending share
sections.summary: Social spending now accounts for over half of the Government's Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: First, social spending now accounts for over half of the Government's Budget.

sections.label: New welfare state form
sections.summary: Singapore has a chance to establish a new form of the welfare state with generous subsidies targeted as practically as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In fact, Singapore has a chance to establish a new form of the welfare state – where generous subsidies are as targeted as practically possible to keep faith with a progressive structure.

sections.label: Budget size comparison
sections.summary: With a Government Budget more than 18% of GDP, Singapore is still below the United States and France.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Second, with the Government Budget that is more than 18% of our gross domestic product (GDP), Singapore is still below the United States (US) and France.

sections.label: Social compact tax burden
sections.summary: The second element of the social compact is that the market stops where social needs arise and the tax burden falls most heavily on the rich.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The second element of our social compact, therefore, is that the market stops where social needs arise, and that the tax burden falls most heavily on the rich as a form of public duty and equity.

sections.label: Research and social compact questions
sections.summary: Questions are asked on enabling longitudinal and local research on social intervention and on keeping Singaporeans understanding stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One, how is the Government enabling more longitudinal and local research to understand what social intervention works and what does not for our different groups of underprivileged Singaporeans in need?

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Two, how can we keep Singaporeans, especially our younger people, understanding the version of stability, self-reliance and social mobility that will work for our people, and how can this be done to build a stronger social compact in the Foward SG efforts?

sections.label: Unwed single mothers' median income
sections.summary: In 2017, unwed single mothers under 35 earned a median monthly income of $600 from work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Previous statistics show that in 2017, unwed single mothers under 35 earn a median monthly income of $600 from work.

sections.label: Income statistics and relief eligibility
sections.summary: The passage asks for new income statistics and whether these mothers could claim Working Mother's Child Relief and Parenthood tax rebates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Are there any new statistics on the median and average monthly income of single unwed mothers?

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, to help them in their role as single mothers supporting their own family, could we consider allowing them to claim the Working Mother's Child Relief and Parenthood tax rebates?

sections.label: LPA portal progress and safeguards
sections.summary: The passage asks about the LPA online portal's progress, protocols against donee abuses, and MSF partnerships to raise awareness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: As such, can the Minister for MSF share on: one, the progress of our new LPA online portal and how much has it spurred adoption; two, the protocols and processes to ensure that abuses by donees can be proactively identified and minimised; and three, how can MSF partner other Government agencies and the media to increase awareness so as to encourage more Singaporeans to do up their LPAs?

sections.label: Nationwide programme for 5,000 children
sections.summary: The passage states that today this is a nationwide programme supporting 5,000 children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Today, this is a nationwide programme supporting 5,000 children.

sections.label: NSF allowance range by vocation
sections.summary: For full-time National Servicemen, allowances start at $580 and go up to $1,280 or more, depending on vocation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With full-time National Servicemen (NSFs), allowances start at $580, going up to $1,280 or more, depending on vocation.

sections.label: Home Caregiving Grant and prison pay
sections.summary: The passage states the Home Caregiving Grant pays $200 and inmates get 30 cents to $2.60 per hour at prison workshops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, the Home Caregiving Grant pays $200.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Inmates get 30 cents to $2.60 per hour at prison workshops.

sections.label: ComCare disbursement time
sections.summary: ComCare disbursements take four weeks on average, or up to six weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: From the Parliamentary Questions I have asked, ComCare disbursements take four weeks, on average, or up to six weeks to disburse.

sections.label: SSO general manager role
sections.summary: In each ComLink town, MSF's SSO general manager acts as social services integrator, assessing family needs and coordinating partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In each ComLink town, MSF's SSO general manager plays the role of a social services integrator – assessing the needs of each family, coordinating with the alliance of partners, such as schools, job centres, the Housing and Development Board (HDB), Police and so forth, to meet those needs.

sections.label: Need for competent integrator
sections.summary: Each family assessed to be in need requires a competent social service integrator who is a trained case manager.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Each family assessed to be in need will require a competent social service integrator who is the trained case manager, able to do the heavy lifting to identify root issues and solutions.

sections.label: Commitment needed for ComLink
sections.summary: ComLink's success requires Government resourcing and agency partners committing beyond lip service, plus willingness to share information and track outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For ComLink to succeed, there must be a commitment to resource by the Government, not only for tangible needs like headcounts, skills training, but also for different agency partners to commit beyond lip service, to get that needed flexible job, financial assistance, preschool placements and so forth to families who need them to move along; and a willingness to share information, track actions and outcomes.

sections.label: ComLink scaling and volunteer shortage
sections.summary: ComLink will be scaled up, but there have been implementation challenges from a shortage of volunteers for needs assessments in some localities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am very happy to know ComLink will be scaled up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand though that there have been implementation challenges from a shortage of volunteers to help with needs assessments in some localities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And for this, I propose that MSF tap on graduated beneficiaries of various social service organisations to bolster the befriending efforts and offer a stipend for their time and contribution.

sections.label: Fund launch and disbursements
sections.summary: The Fund was launched in June 2005 and in FY2021 amounted to $2.4 billion, disbursing around $177 million to about 100,000 individuals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Fund was launched in June 2005 and in FY2021, it amounted to $2.4 billion, disbursing around $177 million to about 100,000 individuals, a non-trivial number, including cash assistance for a shorter as well as longer duration.

sections.label: Government spending on this item
sections.summary: The Government spent about $1 billion on this item in 2018, and this will more than double in the near future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: In 2018, the Government spent about $1 billion on this item.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: In the near future, this will more than double.

sections.label: Childcare fee caps and ComCare payouts
sections.summary: Fee caps for anchor and partner operator childcare and infant care centres were lowered, kindergarten fee caps were lowered, and the ComCare Endowment Fund was topped up by $300 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: When The Straits Times reported in October 2022 that several preschools would be increasing fees for 2023 due to rising costs, I was worried for our young families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: I thus felt assured when the Government promptly announced thereafter that from 1 January this year, full-day childcare and infant care fee caps for Anchor Operator (AOP) and partner operator centres, like PCF Sparkletots Preschool and My First Skool will instead be lowered by $40, excluding Goods and Services Tax (GST).

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: Kindergarten fee caps for anchor operator centres will also be lowered by $10, excluding GST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the ComCare Endowment Fund has been topped up by $300 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: What is the impact this has on ComCare's dollar payouts and the number of people assisted?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: From ComCare's reports, it appears that individuals on average received Short-to-Medium Term Assistance (SMTA) worth $1,700 a year in 2021, $2,300 in 2020, $1,600 in 2019, and $1,400 in 2018, and $1,300 in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Annual growth is at about 7%, which is less than the increase in Government revenue and Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) over the same period.

sections.label: Flexible treatment of household applications
sections.summary: An MSF report states that 40% of households are already having their applications treated flexibly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: According to an MSF report, 40% of households are already having their applications treated flexibly.

sections.label: ComLink for families in rental flats
sections.summary: ComLink was announced in 2019 to bring together SSOs, Government agencies, charities, grassroots organisations and other community partners to help families with children living in public rental flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Chairman, to better help vulnerable, lower-income families, it is crucial to deliver coordinated and family-centric assistance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I was very glad when ComLink was announced in 2019 to bring together SSOs, Government agencies, charities, grassroots organisations and other community partners to help families with children living in public rental flats.

sections.label: Centralisation of backroom integration
sections.summary: At last year's Committee of Supply, Minister Desmond Lee said the Government would strengthen backroom integration across agencies, consolidate common systems and processes where possible and manage them centrally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: At last year's Committee of Supply (COS), Minister Desmond Lee mentioned that the Government would "strengthen backroom integration across agencies", consolidate common systems and processes where possible and manage them centrally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry provide an update on the centralisation process?

sections.label: KiFAS coverage for religious kindergartens
sections.summary: KiFAS would not be extended to children attending kindergartens run by religious entities such as mosques and churches, and the scheme's coverage is hoped to be extended beyond MOE Kindergartens and kindergartens run by AOPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Naturally, their choices would be kindergartens run by religious entities, such as mosques and churches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, this choice can be out of reach for parents who do not have the financial means to do so because the KiFAS would not be extended to their children if they were to attend such institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope that the scheme's coverage can be extended beyond MOE Kindergartens and kindergartens run by AOPs.

sections.label: Staff-child ratio and group sizes
sections.summary: Studies show higher staff-child ratios and smaller group sizes contribute to children's health, safety, interactions and development outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, studies show that a higher staff-child ratio and smaller group sizes contribute to the health, safety, better staff-child interactions and better development outcomes in children.

sections.label: Current staff-child ratio
sections.summary: The current staff-child ratio is one to five.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The current staff-child ratio is one to five.

sections.label: Preschool attrition and educator pay
sections.summary: ECDA said annual attrition was 10% to 15% in a workforce of about 23,000, and preschool educators' pay is set to rise 10% to 30%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In October 2022, ECDA said the annual attrition rate in the sector has been between 10% and 15% over the last few years, in a workforce of about 23,000 people.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note that preschool educators' pay is set to rise by 10% to 30%, amidst a review of working conditions.

sections.label: Starting salaries for preschool graduates
sections.summary: MSF announced starting salaries for fresh graduates joining anchor preschool operators will increase to at least $2,800.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Last year, MSF announced that the starting salaries for fresh graduates joining anchor preschool operators will increase to at least $2,800.

sections.label: Adult disability services and hubs
sections.summary: The passage asks what has moved for employable adults with disabilities and those needing more care, and how many can benefit from the Enabling Business Hub and Enabling Services Hub.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: One key concern of the sector has always been the lack of sufficient services in the adult disability space.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: What has moved for adults with disabilities at the two ends of the spectrum – adults who are employable and adults who are not suitable for paid employment and need more care?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: The proposed Enabling Business Hub and the Enabling Services Hub have been hailed as the two key pilots to address the needs of these two categories of adults.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: How many adults with different abilities can benefit?

sections.label: Masterplan execution leadership team
sections.summary: MSF should appoint an execution leadership team, convene regular sessions, and develop a dashboard and accountability report.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: To inject confidence and to ensure the masterplan stays updated and relevant, MSF should appoint an execution leadership team, convene regular sessions, develop and communicate a dashboard and accountability report.

sections.label: Speaker's son with Down's Syndrome
sections.summary: The speaker says his son has Down's Syndrome and has been diagnosed to be on the autism spectrum.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, my son has Down's Syndrome and has been diagnosed to be on the autism spectrum.

sections.label: Uneven awareness and Enabling Masterplan
sections.summary: The speaker says differing dynamics among advocates may lead to uneven awareness and support, and is grateful for the Enabling Masterplan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There are also different dynamics among the advocates and activists, which may lead to uneven awareness and support structures for different disability groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am therefore grateful that the Government has taken the massive effort to put together different pieces and come up with the concept of the Enabling Masterplan.

sections.label: Framework for different disability groups
sections.summary: The speaker says he does not expect the Government to do everything immediately and believes a framework addressing different groups would be meaningful.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am not expecting the Government to do everything or for things to be done immediately.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There needs to be a whole-of-society effort and involvement, a point which I will touch on later, but I believe it would be meaningful for a framework that dives into specifics for different groups, assessing how successful some measures are, addressing what the challenges are and continually developing the infrastructure of support for PwDs and their families.

sections.label: Dr Chen's holistic healthcare approach
sections.summary: Dr Chen developed a holistic healthcare approach for ageing caregivers and their adult children with intellectual disabilities, addressing social issues and bringing stakeholders together.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Dr Chen had developed a holistic healthcare approach for ageing caregivers and their adult children with intellectual disabilities, addressing also social issues and bringing together multidisciplinary stakeholders on the same platform.

sections.label: Action for Alliance formation
sections.summary: The speaker says the formation of the Action for Alliance for Caregivers of PwDs is encouraging.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The formation of the Action for Alliance (AfA) for Caregivers of PwDs, for example, is encouraging.

sections.label: PAP.SG submission on ageing
sections.summary: The speaker says he put up a 2019 PAP.SG submission on ageing, which called for better caregiver support and a policy review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2019, PAP.SG – then under the leadership of you, Chairman – I put up a submission to the Government with proposals on various aspects of ageing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In one segment of the paper, it was noted that society should provide better support to caregivers including those from the extended family members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Having proper caregiver support within the family can be instrumental for the well-being of our frail seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: We believe that our society have an obligation to do more for the caregivers." Amongst other things, the paper called for a review of policies to strengthen the role that the extended family can play in supporting seniors I believe, and this can include caregiver leave and Flexible Work Arrangements (FWAs).

sections.label: Support for caregivers of PwDs
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes ground-up efforts like AfA caregiver projects and asks for updates and whether they can be scaled up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: We also need support from other people in the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is therefore heartening to note that there had been efforts like the projects carried out by the AfA for Caregivers of PwDs to support caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I believe ground-up efforts like this should be encouraged.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am therefore interested to hear about the update on the projects of the AfA and would like to know if the efforts can be scaled up to benefit more in the community.

sections.label: Continuing education for PwDs
sections.summary: In 2021 the Enabling Masterplan Work Group recommended strengthening continuing education for PwDs through curated courses and enhanced ODP training grants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: Chairman, in 2021, the Enabling Masterplan Work Group recommended for the Government to strengthen the ecosystem for continuing education for PwDs by increasing the number of curated courses in sectors with growth opportunities and enhance the Open Door Programme (ODP) training grant to offer better support in specialised training.

sections.label: Employment rate of PwDs
sections.summary: The average resident employment rate for PwDs aged 15 to 64 rose from 28.2% to 30.1% between FY2018 and FY2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: Chairman, according to the annual Comprehensive Labour Force survey, the average resident employment rate for PwDs aged 15 to 64 has risen from 28.2% to 30.1% from FY2018 to FY2020.

sections.label: PwD employment target and donations
sections.summary: The speaker asks for assessment of efforts toward the Ministry's 40% PwD employment target by 2030, noting annual donations averaged about $3 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: What is the assessment of our efforts to date, to reach the Ministry's target of 40% employment amongst PwDs by 2030?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Over the past five years, the average annual donations collected amounted to about $3 billion.

sections.label: Extension of tax deduction rate
sections.summary: In this year's Budget, the 250% tax deduction rate was extended for another three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In this year's Budget, the tax deduction rate of 250% was extended for another three years.

sections.label: Enabling and compensating social workers
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister how MSF enables, empowers and compensates social workers to journey with families and persons in their care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I would like to ask Minister how is MSF enabling, empowering and compensating our social workers so that they can meaningfully journey with families and persons in their care?

sections.label: Corporate incentives for heartwork
sections.summary: MSF is asked how it plans to incentivise and encourage corporates to join in the "heartwork".

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How does MSF plan to incentivise and encourage corporates to join in the "heartwork"?

sections.label: Empowering SSAs, Tote Board fund
sections.summary: MSF is asked to require salary-practice audits at IPC renewal and whether the Tote Board Social Service Sector Fund will be renewed and enhanced for impact evaluation headcount.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: How can we empower our SSAs to professionalise and scale effective interventions better?

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: I have three recommendations and that is for MSF to require an audit of salary practices each time an organisation renews its Institution of a Public Character (IPC) status.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: I do not have enough time, but I believe these recommendations will enable SSAs to be more self-reliant in the long run by helping them to build up their capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: So, to this end, I would like to ask if the Tote Board Social Service Sector Fund will be renewed to continue supporting SSAs in their efforts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: And will MSF consider also enhancing this funding programme to cater additional budget for impact evaluation headcount?

sections.label: SSA self-reliance, special school reserves
sections.summary: MSF's long-term goal is a vibrant SSA community less reliant on public funding, citing special school reserves unlocked for parent charities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: In the long run, it must be the goal of MSF to have a vibrant and resourceful SSA community that is able to do more with less reliance on public funding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I recall vividly how former Education Minister, now Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, strategically unlocked the highly MOE-controlled reserves of special schools to allow their parent charities to pay for their share of the building costs of the new schools; much to the relief and gratitude of the charities.

sections.label: Community Silver Trust matching limits
sections.summary: The Community Silver Trust matches only 40% of funds for recurrent operating expenses, with the remaining 60% matched only for new projects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Community Silver Trust (CST), for instance, allows for donation matching for only 40% of funds raised, to pay for "recurrent operating expenses".

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The remaining 60% can only be matched if there are "new projects".

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The current CST design shapes charities to do some funny things, to keep thinking of new projects each year to qualify for the matching, when there are ongoing existing programmes that need to be paid for, such as for the disabled and elderly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, it is not useful to the charity partners.

sections.label: Underpaid social service professionals
sections.summary: Social service professionals are in greater demand than ever yet remain underrated, underappreciated and underpaid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Each year, the Graduate Employment Survey shows that our graduates are more and more in demand by the market and that those in greatest demand are, logically, often paid high salaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: A paradox is this: in light of the rising stresses faced by our people as well as the increased emotional fragility, social service professionals are in greater demand than ever before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Yet, they remain underrated and underappreciated, and I would say, underpaid.

sections.label: Size of social service sector
sections.summary: The sector is enormous, with more than 15,000 social workers, therapists, psychologists, nurses, special education teachers, early intervention teachers, social work associates and nursing aides.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: The sector is enormous: more than 15,000 social workers, therapists, psychologists, nurses, special education teachers, early intervention teachers, social work associates, nursing aides and the list goes on.

sections.label: ForwardSG social compact priorities
sections.summary: The ForwardSG exercise found Singaporeans want to help less fortunate citizens, focusing on strong families, social service sector and partnerships.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In seeking a refreshed social compact through the ForwardSG exercise, we have heard many speak of their desire to help less fortunate Singaporeans nurture and build better lives, to forge an inclusive and caring Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will build on these aspirations of Singaporeans and focus their energies in three very important areas: firstly, building strong families and uplifting families that require additional support; secondly, strengthening the social service sector to deliver services that meet the needs of families; and thirdly, weaving an extensive tapestry of support around families by expanding partnerships across society in a renewed social compact.

sections.label: FFL @ Community expansion
sections.summary: FFL @ Community will expand to nine towns by end of this year and all towns by 2025, benefiting 4,000 couples and 20,000 parents yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: More recently, it intensified ground outreach in Choa Chu Kang and Yishun, by offering localised marriage, parenting and even grandparenting programmes under the FFL @ Community initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that FFL will expand this initiative to nine towns by the end of this year and to all towns by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: An expected 4,000 couples and 20,000 parents will benefit from these programmes every year from 2025 onwards.

sections.label: Government benefits for children
sections.summary: Government benefits supporting children's growth include subsidies for education, healthcare, infant care, childcare, foreign domestic worker levy concession and the CDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Hence, we extend Government benefits that support the growth and development of their children as we do to other children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: These include subsidies for education, healthcare, infant care and childcare, the foreign domestic worker levy concession and the CDA.

sections.label: Pre-planning public education campaign
sections.summary: Over 10,000 online applications were made, and MSF, MOH and the Public Service Division will launch a public education campaign to promote pre-planning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: More than 10,000 applications have been made online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: MSF, MOH and the Public Service Division will be launching a public education campaign to promote pre-planning.

sections.label: KidSTART nationwide scaling
sections.summary: KidSTART has supported over 6,200 children from lower-income families with good results, and will be scaled up nationwide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: KidSTART has supported over 6,200 children from lower-income families thus far and we have seen good results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: As announced by Deputy Prime Minister Wong in the Budget, we will be scaling up KidSTART nationwide.

sections.label: First Enabling Services Hub launch
sections.summary: The first Enabling Services Hub will be launched in Tampines West Community Centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: On this note, I am happy to announce the launch of the first Enabling Services Hub in Tampines West Community Centre.

sections.label: Tote Board Fund commitment
sections.summary: The Tote Board's largest commitment since the Fund began complements about $400 million a year in Government funding for key social programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This is the Tote Board's largest commitment since the inception of the Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: It complements the Government's funding of about $400 million a year to support key social programmes.

sections.label: Social service salary increases
sections.summary: More than 20,000 employees, including social workers, psychologists, early intervention educators and care workers, are expected to see FY2023 increases of 4% to 15%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: When implemented, more than 20,000 employees, including social workers, psychologists, early intervention educators and care workers, are expected to see increases by between 4% and 15% in FY2023.

sections.label: Sector Evaluation Framework metrics
sections.summary: The Sector Evaluation Framework, launched in 2021, gives SSAs, funders and public agencies a common language and outcome metric to articulate impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The Sector Evaluation Framework, launched in 2021, provides SSAs, funders and public agencies a common language and outcome metric to articulate impact.

sections.label: NCSS sustainable philanthropy work
sections.summary: NCSS works with the National Volunteer and Philanthropy Centre to define and measure businesses' impact on social causes, such as the Change for Charity initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: NCSS champions sustainable philanthropy and is working with the National Volunteer and Philanthropy Centre, which recently launched its Corporate Purpose Framework, to define and measure businesses' impact on social causes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: One example of sustainable philanthropy is the Change for Charity initiative, where businesses enable customers to donate to Community Chest conveniently when they make payments.

sections.label: Family hardiness and mothers' hope
sections.summary: The study found family hardiness, including adaptability and sense of control, bolstered mothers' short-term hope and reduced longer-term mental health issue risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The study found that building family hardiness, which includes the family's ability to adapt and the family's sense of control over the situation, helped to bolster mothers' hope in the short-term and reduce the risk of longer-term mental health issues.

sections.label: GUSTO study on responsiveness
sections.summary: The GUSTO study showed mothers' responsiveness to their child's needs in infancy affects the child's school readiness and academic performance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The GUSTO study by researchers from the National University Health System, KK Women's and Children's Hospital, NUS and the Agency for Science, Technology and Research showed that mothers' responsiveness to their child's needs in infancy makes a difference to the child's readiness for school and academic performance.

sections.label: Support for low-income Malay/Muslim families
sections.summary: ComLink, KidSTART and Project DIAN@M3 involve community partners to help low-income and Malay/Muslim families in rental flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Key programmes such as ComLink and KidSTART will involve community partners and help low-income families, including our Malay/Muslim families, achieve stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Through Project DIAN@M3, more effective and integrated support is provided to Malay/Muslim families staying in rental flats, by connecting them to the national and community programmes for education, employment, social support and health.

sections.label: Project Pathfinder and social service partners
sections.summary: Project Pathfinder pairs ITE College East students with SAF volunteer mentors, and MSF dedicated 2023 to celebrating social service partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: For instance, through Project Pathfinder by volunteers from the Singapore Armed Forces, students at the Institute of Technical Education College East are paired with mentors who provide guidance towards attaining resilience and equipping them with knowledge and discipline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: To highlight their efforts, MSF has dedicated 2023 as the Year of Celebrating Social Service Partners.

sections.label: Singapore Made for Families
sections.summary: The passage states that a strong social compact can build a Singapore Made for Families supporting stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Together, we can build a Singapore Made for Families, where our strong social compact supports all families in achieving stability, self-reliance and keeps social mobility alive.

sections.label: Preschool infant and playgroup places
sections.summary: About 7,000 of the full-day preschool places AOPs are creating over two years will be for infant care and playgroup.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To better support families who require infant and playgroup services, some 7,000 of the full-day preschool places that AOPs are creating over the next two years will be for infant care and playgroup programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The number of qualified educators has tripled from 2,100 in 2017 to 6,400 in 2022 and we will continue to do more.

sections.label: Revised EYDF timeline
sections.summary: The review is ongoing and the revised EYDF is slated to be ready by October 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The review is currently ongoing and the revised EYDF is slated to be ready by October 2023.

sections.label: Dual-income families in preschools
sections.summary: About 85% of Singaporean children enrolled in preschools come from dual-income families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Today, about 85% of Singaporean children enrolled in preschools come from dual-income families.

sections.label: Preschool enrolment and capacity
sections.summary: About nine in 10 children aged three to six are enrolled, and 22,000 more full-day preschool places will be created over two years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Today, around nine in 10 Singaporean children aged three to six years are enrolled in preschools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: At the national level, there are currently enough preschool places to accommodate every resident child aged three and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: However, we recognise that capacity is tighter in some areas, and this is why we are working with AOPs to increase the sector's capacity and create 22,000 more full-day preschool places over the next two years.

sections.label: Early childhood educator numbers
sections.summary: There are over 24,000 certified early childhood educators, with 10% to 15% annual attrition, and at least 2,500 more are needed by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Currently, there are over 24,000 certified early childhood educators, with an annual sector attrition rate of around 10% to 15% over the past few years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will need at least another 2,500 educators by 2025.

sections.label: Educator salary ranges and recruitment
sections.summary: ECDA provided recommended salary ranges for the sector, and the number of educators joining has risen 18%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: ECDA has also provided recommended salary ranges that the rest of the sector can refer to when reviewing remuneration packages for their educators.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: I am glad to share that we have since seen an 18% increase in the number of educators who have joined the sector.

sections.label: Preschool fee caps and median fees
sections.summary: Government-supported preschools must adhere to fee caps, which brought median preschool fees down from $800 in 2016 to $760 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To make preschool more affordable, we fund Government-supported preschools to adhere to fee caps and other quality requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: These fee caps have brought down median fees in the preschool sector, from $800 in 2016 to $760 in 2022.

sections.label: Government early childhood spending
sections.summary: Government spending on the early childhood sector rose almost six-fold, from $320 million in 2013 to about $1.9 billion in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Over the last decade, the Government's spending on the early childhood sector has increased almost six-fold, from $320 million in 2013 to about $1.9 billion in 2022.

sections.label: KidSTART enrolment with hospitals
sections.summary: The Government will work with KKH and the National University Hospital on protocols to identify and encourage eligible mothers-to-be to sign up for KidSTART.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To achieve this expansion, we will be working with KKH and the National University Hospital to develop protocols to allow us to systematically identify and encourage more eligible mothers-to-be to sign up for KidSTART.

sections.label: Priority enrolment for lower-income children
sections.summary: Every child from a lower-income household will have priority enrolment in AOP preschools so they can be enrolled as soon as possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Every child from a lower-income household will have priority enrolment in AOP preschools so that they can be enrolled as soon as possible.

sections.label: Expanding early intervention capacity
sections.summary: ECDA will expand EIPIC and the PPIP programme by 1,400 places over the next two years for children needing medium to high-level EI support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: ECDA will expand the capacity of the Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children, or EIPIC, as well as the Enhanced Pilot for Private Intervention Providers programme, or PPIP, by 1,400 places over the next two years so that more children requiring medium to high-levels of EI support can receive timely intervention.

sections.label: Subsidies and PPIP enrolment
sections.summary: A middle-income family can expect to pay around $190 per month after subsidies, and the plans aim to serve 80% of children needing medium to high EI support by 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As an illustration, a middle-income family can expect to pay around $190 per month after subsidies, less than half of what they are paying today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: With this, we hope that more families who are waiting for a place in EIPIC will enrol their children in PPIP instead.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: These plans will help us generate sufficient Government-funded places to serve 80% of children requiring medium to high levels of EI support by 2027, up from 60% today.

sections.label: Inclusion coordinators in preschools
sections.summary: There are around 1,000 trained inclusion coordinators, and the aim is to appoint an inclusion coordinator in every preschool by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Parents have also shared that an inclusive learning environment has been beneficial for children with developmental needs, as well as their typically developing peers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We currently have around 1,000 trained inclusion coordinators.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: They will play a crucial role in preschools to refer families to relevant EI resources and work with fellow educators to identify children with potential developmental needs for further assessment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We are making good progress towards our aim of appointing an inclusion coordinator in every preschool by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Last year, we launched a Parents' Guide to provide parents and caregivers with information on EI services, as well as caregiver training and support at key milestones along their caregiving journey.

sections.label: Infant care settings
sections.summary: Most infants are cared for in a home-based setting by caregivers, while around one in five infants are in centre-based infant care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Today, most infants are cared for in a home-based setting by caregivers, such as parents and family members, while around one in five infants are in centre-based infant care.

sections.label: Celebrating social service partners
sections.summary: For the next three years, MSF will celebrate the good work of those who deliver social good every day, starting with 2023 as the Year of Celebrating Social Service Partners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For the next three years, MSF will shine the spotlight on and celebrate the good work of those who deliver social good every day – starting with 2023 as the Year of Celebrating Social Service Partners – to recognise the integral contributions of platform from within and beyond the social service platform sector, who work with us and with each other, to build strong families and a caring society.

sections.label: Fourth Enabling Masterplan launch
sections.summary: The fourth Enabling Masterplan, EMP2030, was launched in August last year using the same partnership approach.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The same partnership approach also informed our fourth Enabling Masterplan, EMP2030, which we launched in August last year.

sections.label: Goals across 14 Focal Areas
sections.summary: Clear, tangible goals across 14 Focal Areas are penned for the first time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: For the first time, clear, tangible goals across 14 Focal Areas are penned.

sections.label: Special education needs students in mainstream schools
sections.summary: About 80% of students with mild to moderate special education needs attend mainstream schools today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Today, about 80% of students with mild to moderate special education needs attend mainstream schools.

sections.label: First Enabling Services Hub launch
sections.summary: The first Enabling Services Hub will launch in the coming months with SPD in Tampines West Community Centre.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: First, the Enabling Services Hubs (ESH), this will take a regional approach towards strengthening support for PwDs within the community, making our local communities more inclusive.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The first ESH will be launched in the coming months in collaboration with Society for the Physically Disabled (SPD) in Tampines West Community Centre.

sections.label: Target employment rate for PwDs
sections.summary: The EBH will contribute to an aspirational employment rate target for PwDs of 40% by 2030, up from 31% today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Along with other measures, the EBH will contribute to our aspirational target employment rate for PwDs of 40% by 2030, up from 31% today.

sections.label: Adding sheltered workshop places
sections.summary: 100 sheltered workshop places will be added by early 2024, bringing total capacity to 1,800.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: This will enable more PwDs who are not yet ready for or unable to take up open employment to receive work skills training and work therapy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We will be adding 100 sheltered workshop places by early 2024, bringing the total capacity to 1,800.

sections.label: Project 3i caregiver support
sections.summary: Project 3i has supported over 2,700 caregivers since November 2021 and will expand to two more constituencies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Since its launch in November 2021, Project 3i has supported over 2,700 caregivers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Over 130 community volunteers and caregivers have been trained to support other caregivers of PwDs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Going forward, the AfA will expand Project 3i to two more constituencies so that more caregivers can benefit from the support network.

sections.label: ComLink islandwide expansion
sections.summary: ComLink expanded from four pilot towns in 2019 to some 21 communities, with 264 programmes and services provided to date.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: From four pilot towns in 2019, we have in the past two years expanded ComLink islandwide to some 21 ComLink communities, each supported by an SSO.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Together, community partners and Government agencies have provided 264 ComLink programmes and services to date, including those such as financial literacy programmes, enrichment activities, sporting activities and so on.

sections.label: Volunteer befrienders and families
sections.summary: Some 760 volunteer befrienders work with some 3,500 families.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Today, we have some 760 volunteer befrienders working with some 3,500 families.

sections.label: Streamlining befriending and case support
sections.summary: Befriending functions will be streamlined into a single action plan, starting with 60 families in Jalan Besar.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: These families are also visited by befrienders from different agencies and organisations, each sharing their own programmes and criteria, and this creates plenty of confusion and adds to these families' bandwidth tax.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We will streamline functions such as outreach, befriending and case support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The befriender will organise interventions into a single coherent action plan and work with families to achieve their goals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We started this approach with some 60 families in Jalan Besar over the last few months and families have found it beneficial.

sections.label: ComCare financial assistance
sections.summary: ComCare supports lower-income households with financial assistance for basic daily expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: ComCare supports lower-income households with financial assistance to meet their basic daily expenses.

sections.label: ComCare application simplifications
sections.summary: ComCare applicants who are account holders need not resubmit certain information, and scheme bundles give automatic referrals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: ComCare applicants who are also account holders need not separately submit information on HDB rental, Singapore Power utilities and S&CC by the Town Council.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: For instance, with the introduction of ComCare scheme bundles, eligible ComCare beneficiaries are now automatically referred and/or qualified for Government assistance for education, healthcare, student care and childcare.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Mr Leon Perera will be glad to know that we have also enhanced the SupportGoWhere portal to allow online applications for ComCare SMTA, so that applicants need not go to SSOs in person to apply.

sections.label: SG Enable ESH launch
sections.summary: SG Enable will launch the first ESH with SPD in Tampines West Community Centre in the coming months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To strengthen our support for them, SG Enable will be launching the first ESH in collaboration with SPD in Tampines West Community Centre in the coming months.

sections.label: Rental flat families agency
sections.summary: Families in rental flats receiving aid also have agency and can uplift themselves and help others.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Boomer me did not know that this is called a charm, by the way.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We often hear of families living in rental flats being beneficiaries of aid and support and overlook the fact that these families, too, have agency.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: They, too, can be empowered, take active steps to uplift themselves and even help fellow families in need.

sections.label: Call for inclusive Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker cites S17 Community Kitchen and Helen Keller, calling on all to build a caring, inclusive Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Mr Raymond Khoo and his team at the S17 Community Kitchen is one great example.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: So, in Lengkok Bahru, I see remarkable resilience, a great deal of love and a thriving kampung spirit!

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: But to be a truly caring and inclusive society, we must look beyond our own.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: A quote by disability rights advocate Helen Keller is fitting, "Alone we can do so little but, together, we can do so much".

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: So, right now, let me call upon every Member in this Chamber, every Singaporean, young and old, regardless of race, language or religion, to come together so that we can build an even more caring and inclusive Singapore for our next generation.

sections.label: Early childhood sector staffing
sections.summary: An additional 2,500 persons are needed to join the early childhood sector by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As I have mentioned in my main speech, we would need an additional 2,500 persons to join the early childhood sector by 2025.

sections.label: ComCare assistance review and inflation
sections.summary: ComCare SMTA and Long-Term Assistance were reviewed in August 2022, raising SMTA from $600 to $640.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The ComCare SMTA and the Long-Term Assistance were just reviewed in August 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: So, we raised that from $600 to $640, and have higher cash assistance for the Long-Term Assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: But we must continue to monitor this current increase in inflation, which is not the usual one, creeping slowly, but given the circumstances that are faced by people all over the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We will look at this and, if the need arises, we will certainly increase the support to our ComCare recipients.

sections.label: ComLink policy sandboxes
sections.summary: Part of ComLink is about policy sandboxes, such as the 60 Jalan Besar families taking an upstream approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: The last point on experimentation, I think the Member would be very seized to find that part of ComLink is exactly about that – for us to have an area carved out that we can do policy sandboxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: For instance, the point about the 60 Jalan Besar families taking on this upstream approach.

sections.label: Number of befrienders
sections.summary: The speaker states there are now more than 700 befrienders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: As I mentioned in my speech, today, we have more than 700 befrienders.

sections.label: Additional 100 job places
sections.summary: The speaker asks what kind of jobs the additional 100 over places added this year are.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: The second question is, what kind of jobs are the additional 100 over places that you mentioned would be added this year?

sections.label: Sheltered workshop jobs
sections.summary: The additional 100 spaces are the type of jobs typically found in a sheltered workshop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: The additional 100 spaces that we are talking about would be the type of jobs that we typically can find in a sheltered workshop.

sections.label: Befriender training curriculum
sections.summary: Befrienders are committed and go through a full training curriculum with the SSOs, including a tiered training roadmap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: What we have done is to make sure that the befrienders are committed and they also go through a full training curriculum with the SSOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: There is a training roadmap for our ComLink befrienders, which includes topics like understanding the social service landscape in Singapore, family and domestic violence awareness training and also ComLink befriending training, which is tiered into two different levels – Tier 1 and Tier 2.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Those components about dos and do nots for home visits, befriending philosophy, building rapport, sensing needs, nudging families – our befrienders are trained as part of this curriculum in those competencies and skill sets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: To that end, I will assure the Member that the befrienders are well equipped to take on the challenges in being a part of this – I agree with her – this mammoth and gargantuan endeavour to really make a change in the rental flat family landscape.

sections.label: ComLink Alliance Workgroup meetings
sections.summary: The ComLink Alliance Workgroup steering committee for each town meets monthly, with 21 leads for 21 towns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: In terms of the planning that goes on behind the scenes, the ComLink Alliance Workgroup that is the steering committee for each town meets very frequently – monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: We have 21 of such leads there are leading the efforts in each of the 21 towns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: In terms of how we connect with the different partners within the community, this is a central node.

sections.label: Community partners in ComLink
sections.summary: Community nodes such as the grassroots are plugged into the ComLink Alliance Workgroup and are a source of new volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: They too feature very strongly in ComLink because they are a good source of new volunteers who might be interested, who might want to be a part of this ComLink journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Those typical nodes that you find in the community landscape in each town – for instance, the grassroots – they are also plugged into this ComLink Alliance Workgroup.

sections.label: MSF and SportCares programmes
sections.summary: MSF colleagues helped create academic and sporting programmes, including SportCares, which reaches rental flat families through football and basketball.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: What we have done is my MSF colleagues have helped to create a buffet of different offerings of academic programmes, of sporting programmes – for instance, Sport Singapore has this SportCares programme that reaches out to rental flat families through football, basketball and all that.
